This neuron fires at end-of-line sentence terminators (".\n", ").\n", "!\n") that close out business/contact/address/company boilerplate lines (and similarly at the fixed "last edited" phrase), i.e. it's a line-boundary punctuation detector in that register — the same ".\n" token strongly *suppresses* it in other contexts (dimension lists, dates, bios).

Fires on grammatical "glue" tokens at clause junctures — positively on modals/auxiliaries, determiners and the relative "that" (or a comma) that open a new predicate/modifier ("might", "can", "that", "a", ", allowing") — and is suppressed by prepositions/conjunctions that merely complete a fixed collocation ("receipt of", "as soon as", "and begin", "when they"); it appears to track function-word type at continuation points rather than any semantic content.
